# Dick Moore

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v4 c11 P24](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0024)</sub>
- **Status:** deceased  <sub>[v4 c31 P28](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0028), [v4 c32 P6](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0006), [v4 c36 P27](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0027)</sub>
- **Role:** sailor and store clerk  <sub>[v4 c11 P24](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0024)</sub>

## Appearance

Dick was a big, handsome fellow with a sea-going streak. His features were remarkably similar to those of his double cousin George, including a rare peculiarity of having one blue eye and one hazel eye. He had a higher color than George and his hair was a shade lighter.

_Sources: [v4 c11 P24](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0024), [v4 c13 P15](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0015), [v4 c32 P12](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0012)_

## Personality

Dick had a selfish, small-minded, and unpleasant nature beneath his handsome looks. He was pleasant and agreeable enough when things went his way, but he possessed a selfish temperament where he passionately pursued whatever he wanted until he obtained it, after which he lost interest. He drank heavily and harbored a vengeful, spiteful streak.

_Sources: [v4 c11 P24](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0024), [v4 c11 P28](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0028), [v4 c21 P46](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0046)_

## History

Dick grew up as the son of Abner Moore and worked as a clerk in his father's store during winters while spending summers at sea. In his youth, he fell obsessively in love with Leslie West due to her beauty and her refusal to have anything to do with him. He pursued her persistently until she agreed to marry him to save her mother from losing her home. Following their marriage, he quickly grew tired of quiet domestic life and set off for Nova Scotia. There he joined his cousin George Moore aboard the ship *Four Sisters* bound for Havana. While in Cuba, Dick contracted yellow fever and died thirteen years prior to the truth being discovered. His cousin George stayed behind to nurse him, was present at his burial, and took his money, watch, and a letter from Leslie to return to her, before suffering an accident that caused loss of memory and led to George being mistaken for Dick for twelve years.

_Sources: [v4 c11 P24](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0024), [v4 c11 P28](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0028), [v4 c21 P46](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0046), [v4 c31 P28](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0028), [v4 c32 P6](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0006), [v4 c33 P9](../source/v04-c33.md#nw-v04-c33-p0009), [v4 c36 P27](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0027)_
